claims.text: The 5.00 SGD is not riding on this case as an uncollected charge: it was charged at 13:33:44 and then reversed at 15:25:40, 'refunded to rider and withheld from driver pending review' (EV-TRIP-05069), and the payments ledger shows payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00 (EV-FARE-05069). The driver's filing asks the tribunal to move that 5.00 back to him. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative and never means 'restore a charge' - it means the filer's claim is not supported and the present state stands. The present state is a completed refund to the rider, and that is where the rider's case rests: the 5.00 refunded to her stays with her unless the driver positively makes out that the fee stands.

POL-NS-23 is the only limb of the driver's case that is not on the face of the platform record, and on that record it is thin. trip_record.in_app_calls is an empty array (EV-TRIP-05069), so no platform call record exists for this trip; the sole call evidence is one chat-log entry, MSG-05069-002 (EV-CHAT-05069), which records the call as 'Outgoing in-app call to rider - not answered (rang 24 s)'. The rider's statement on file - 'He never called me, he only sent messages' - is exactly what that entry says happened: a call was dialled and nothing was answered. The rider's account is therefore not a bare denial set against the record; it matches the record. On this evidence the driver has shown that he dialled, not that the rider was contacted, and the second limb of POL-NS-23 is not made out to the standard that would justify restoring a no-show fee against the rider.

If the tribunal reads POL-NS-23 as satisfied by a dialled-call line, the contact fact is still carried by no call record in the trip file at all: trip_record.in_app_calls is empty (EV-TRIP-05069) and the only support is a text entry in the chat log (EV-CHAT-05069). POL-GEN-26 sends a case to human review where a fact a rule needs cannot be established from the evidence that should carry it, and an escalated amount is held rather than collected - which leaves the rider's refunded 5.00 where it is and puts the driver's claim before a reviewer instead of restoring the charge on this record. I make that argument on completeness, not impairment: the chat log is graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and I do not suggest any issue code fired on it.

claims.text: The driver was physically at the pickup when the arrival event fired. The platform trip record puts auto-arrival from driver GPS at 13:27:15 on 2026-09-17 at Block 216, Serangoon Avenue 4, and the GPS trace corroborates it: the nearest fix (index 12, 13:27:10) sits 0.497 m from the pickup point with a reported horizontal accuracy of 6 m, well inside the 50 m arrival radius that applies to a STANDARD pickup zone, and the trace reports accuracy on every fix so the 25 m accuracy filter is satisfied, not evaded. The arrival test under POL-NS-21 is therefore met on the platform's own evidence, at weight 1.0.

The free wait ran in full before the driver cancelled. Arrival at 13:27:15 starts the 300 s clock under POL-NS-21, so the free wait ended at 13:32:15; the platform logged 'free wait period expired; rider not on board' at 13:32:20 and the driver cancelled at 13:33:40, 385 s after arrival and 85 s after the wait expired. The trace shows the vehicle stationary at the pickup from 13:27:10 to 13:33:40 (speed 0 kph on every fix in that span), so the driver did not merely touch and go; he waited out the free period before cancelling. POL-NS-21 is satisfied and POL-NS-22's precondition - a driver cancellation after the free wait - is met.

The driver discharged the POL-NS-23 contact obligation in both limbs, before cancelling. He sent in-app chat messages at 13:27:40 (MSG-05069-001, 'Hi I'm at Blk 216 drop off') and 13:32:00 (MSG-05069-003, 'Hello?'), and he placed an in-app call at 13:30:15 (MSG-05069-002, channel VOICE_CALL_LOG, 'Outgoing in-app call to rider - not answered (rang 24 s)'). All three entries pre-date trip_record.cancelled_at of 13:33:40. POL-NS-23 expressly accepts 'a voice-call entry in the chat log' as the call limb, and the platform chat log is a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0 whose derived contact check records complete = true, call_count = 1 and obligation_met = true. The clause is satisfied and the fee is not voided.

The rider's counter-statement - 'He never called me, he only sent messages' - is contradicted by the platform's own voice-call record and does not defeat the contact obligation. POL-NS-23 requires that the driver place at least one in-app call, not that the rider answer it; the log records an outgoing call placed at 13:30:15 that rang for 24 s unanswered, which is precisely the situation the clause contemplates. The rider may not have registered the call, but the obligation is judged on the placed call, and the placed call is on the record at weight 1.0.

POL-NS-24 does not assist the rider here. That clause gives a rider a free cancellation only where the driver fails to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes and the rider then cancels; this trip was on-demand, it was cancelled by the driver and not by the rider, and the driver in fact arrived at 13:27:15. Nor can the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit under POL-NS-24 arise, because it is conditioned on a failure to attempt contact and the chat log records an attempted call as well as two messages. There is no driver no-show on this record.

The fee was correctly charged at the policy figure and belongs to the driver. The payments ledger records a 5.00 SGD cancellation fee, category NO_SHOW_CHARGE, with fee_matches_policy = true against the POL-NS-22 schedule of 5.00 SGD, and POL-NS-22 directs that a fee charged after a post-free-wait cancellation is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel. On the merits the driver is owed that 5.00 SGD, and under POL-GEN-03 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

NO_ACTION would be the wrong outcome and would simply entrench the error. The interim reversal at 13:25:40 (recorded as fee_reversed) refunded the 5.00 SGD to the rider and withheld it from the driver, pending this review. POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative: it means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands. Here the driver's claim IS supported - the free wait was served and the contact obligation was met - so leaving the present state standing would leave the driver 5.00 SGD out of pocket on a fee the policy awards him. The driver asks for DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, not for a further or separate payment.

Nothing in this record requires escalation. The two facts the no-show rules turn on - when the driver arrived, and whether he messaged and called before cancelling - are both established by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 (the platform trip record, the GPS trace and the chat log), so POL-GEN-26's condition, a fact the evidence cannot establish, is not met. The contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no 0.95 bar applies; and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling final on a 5.00 SGD no-show, subject only to POL-GEN-21, which is not engaged because no safety indicator appears anywhere on this record.

ruling.explanation:
To the driver and to the rider: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee stands, so the sum already refunded to you, rider, and withheld from you, driver, is returned to the driver. The driver filed, so the outcome is read from his claim against the present state.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. Arrival: the platform trip record logs auto-arrival from the driver's GPS at 13:27:15 on 2026-09-17 at Block 216, Serangoon Avenue 4, and the trace corroborates it — the nearest fix (13:27:10) is 0.497 m from the pickup point at a reported accuracy of 6 m, well inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup, and every fix reports an accuracy so the 25 m filter is satisfied (EV-TRIP-05069, EV-GPS-05069; POL-NS-21).

Free wait: the 300 s free wait runs from arrival under POL-NS-21, so it ended at 13:32:15; the platform logged the wait expired at 13:32:20 and the driver cancelled at 13:33:40 — 385 s after arrival, 85 s past the wait, with the trace showing the vehicle stationary at the pickup throughout. The POL-NS-22 precondition (a driver cancellation after the free wait) is met.

Contact obligation (POL-NS-23): the driver sent in-app messages at 13:27:40 and 13:32:00 and placed an in-app call at 13:30:15 (chat-log entry MSG-05069-002, channel VOICE_CALL_LOG, 'Outgoing in-app call to rider - not answered (rang 24 s)'), all before cancelled_at of 13:33:40. The clause expressly accepts 'a voice-call entry in the chat log' as the call limb, and the chat log is a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0. The obligation is discharged.

THE RIDER'S POINTS. Your statement that he 'never called me, he only sent messages' is answered by the clause itself: POL-NS-23 requires the driver to place a call, not that you answer it, and the platform log records the outgoing call. Your advocate's point that trip_record.in_app_calls is empty (EV-TRIP-05069) does not defeat the limb — the clause names the chat-log voice-call entry as an alternative carrier, and that entry exists. Your advocate's POL-GEN-26 completeness argument is rejected: the clause names the artifact that carries the fact, the chat log is graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and no issue code fired on it, so there is no fact the record cannot establish. POL-NS-24 does not assist you either: it gives a rider a free cancellation where the driver fails to arrive by the scheduled time plus 5 minutes and the rider cancels — this trip was on-demand, the driver arrived, and the driver cancelled.

MONEY. The payments ledger records the fee charged at 5.00 SGD, matching the POL-NS-22 schedule, and records it refunded at 15:25:40 (EV-FARE-05069: payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00; EV-TRIP-05069: fee_reversed). Because the fee is upheld, the 5.00 SGD is owing to the driver: DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

REFERRALS. None. POL-NS-22 produces a referral only where the amount charged is other than 5.00 SGD, and it is exactly 5.00; POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is conditioned on a failure to attempt contact, which did not occur; POL-NS-25's counter is absent from the rider profile and would not reach 3 in any event.

CONFIDENCE AND WHO DECIDES. The deciding facts rest on COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-05069, EV-GPS-05069, EV-CHAT-05069); the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05069-01 carries no deciding fact and does not cap confidence. The contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so the AI ruling is final under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26. No safety indicator appears, so POL-GEN-21 is not engaged.

Both parties: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee on trip TRP-05069 stands, the interim reversal of 2026-09-17 is undone, and the 5.00 SGD is returned to the driver.

Arrival and the free wait (POL-NS-21). The trip record's auto-arrival at 13:27:15 is corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace: the nearest fix (index 12, 13:27:10) sits about 0.5 m from the pickup point with a reported accuracy of 6 m, well inside the 50 m radius that applies to a STANDARD pickup zone, and every fix reports an accuracy so the 25 m filter is satisfied rather than evaded. The 300 s (5-minute) free wait therefore started at 13:27:15 and expired at 13:32:15. The driver cancelled at 13:33:40 — 385 s after arrival and 85 s after the wait expired — and the trace shows the vehicle stationary at the pickup throughout. The free wait was served.

Contact obligation (POL-NS-23). The chat log records a driver message at 13:27:40, an outgoing in-app call at 13:30:15 that rang 24 s unanswered, and a further driver message at 13:32:00 — all before the 13:33:40 cancellation. The clause requires at least one in-app chat message AND at least one in-app call placed before cancelling, and it expressly accepts 'a voice-call entry in the chat log' as the call limb. It tests whether a call was placed, not whether it was answered. The rider is right that the call went unanswered, but that does not void the fee: the rider's account that the driver 'never called' is not borne out, because the call was placed and merely not picked up.

Escalation (POL-GEN-26). The rider asks for human review on the basis that the call fact is unsupported because trip_record.in_app_calls is empty. POL-NS-23 does not require that field — it names the chat log's voice-call entry as an alternative, and that entry is present in a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0. The fact the rule needs is established, so POL-GEN-26's condition is not met and nothing is escalated. (POL-GEN-26 also has no purchase through POL-NS-24: the driver arrived, and it was the driver, not the rider, who cancelled.)

The fee and the outcome (POL-NS-22, POL-GEN-03). The payments ledger records a 5.00 SGD cancellation fee, category NO_SHOW_CHARGE, matching the POL-NS-22 schedule, so it stands and is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel. Because the filer is the driver and the present state already refunded the 5.00 SGD to the rider and recovered it from him, the driver being owed the whole 5.00 SGD means the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both carrying the same figure, 5.00 — the amount this ruling moves back to the driver, not a second payment. No referral arises: the charged amount equals the policy fee (so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not fire), the rider was not owed a POL-NS-24 goodwill credit, and no repeat no-show counter is present on the rider profile (POL-NS-25).

Decision basis. The contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final. The deciding facts rest on artifacts all at weight 1.0 (trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare ledger), so confidence is not capped below 1.0.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: the driver filed to contest the platform's reversal of the 5.00 SGD no-show fee. I find the fee should stand and the driver should be paid it.

The free wait (POL-NS-21). The trip record (EV-TRIP-05069) puts the driver's auto-arrival at Block 216, Serangoon Avenue 4 at 13:27:15, and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-05069) corroborates it: the nearest fix (index 12, 13:27:10) sits 0.5 m from the pickup at a reported accuracy of 6 m, inside the 50 m radius for a STANDARD zone, and every fix reports an accuracy so the 25 m filter is satisfied. The 300-second free wait ran from arrival to 13:32:15; the platform logged the wait expired at 13:32:20 and the driver cancelled at 13:33:40, 385 seconds after arrival, with the trace showing the vehicle stationary at the pickup throughout. The free wait was served in full and POL-NS-22's precondition -- a cancellation after the free wait -- is met.

The contact obligation (POL-NS-23). The chat log (EV-CHAT-05069) records a driver message at 13:27:40 (MSG-05069-001), an outgoing in-app call at 13:30:15 (MSG-05069-002, VOICE_CALL_LOG, 'not answered (rang 24 s)') and a further message at 13:32:00 (MSG-05069-003), all before the 13:33:40 cancellation. The clause expressly accepts 'a voice-call entry in the chat log' as the call limb and requires only that the call be placed, not that it be answered. Both limbs are met and the fee is not voided.

I have answered each surviving claim. The rider's point that the 5.00 SGD is a completed refund that should stay with her under POL-GEN-03's party-relative NO_ACTION is rejected: the driver does make out that the fee stands, so the present state is not the correct one. Her point that the call limb is thin because trip_record.in_app_calls is empty is rejected: POL-NS-23 names the chat-log voice-call entry as a carrier, and her own statement ('he never called me, he only sent messages') is answered by that entry, which shows a call placed to her and not answered. Her POL-GEN-26 escalation point is rejected: every fact the no-show rules need -- when the driver arrived and whether he messaged and called before cancelling -- is established by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-05069, EV-GPS-05069, EV-CHAT-05069), so there is no unestablished fact to escalate. The driver's claims on arrival, the free wait, the contact obligation, POL-NS-24 and the fee amount are accepted.

POL-NS-24 does not assist the rider: the driver arrived, the rider did not cancel, and the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is conditioned on a failure to attempt contact, which did not occur. POL-NS-22's fee-amount check produces no referral (the 5.00 SGD charged on EV-FARE-05069 matches the policy figure of 5.00 SGD), and POL-NS-25 produces none (the rider's profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter).

Outcome. The driver's claim is supported. The figures I used are the 5.00 SGD fee charged at 13:33:44 (EV-FARE-05069, total_charged 5.00, cancellation_fee 5.00) and the 5.00 SGD interim refund recorded at 15:25:40 (EV-FARE-05069, refund_issued_sgd 5.00, EV-TRIP-05069, fee_reversed). Under POL-GEN-03 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd carrying that same figure. The value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, no fraud flag applies, and POL-NS-26 makes this ruling final.

ledger.claim: The 5.00 SGD is not riding on this case as an uncollected charge: it was charged at 13:33:44 and then reversed at 15:25:40, 'refunded to rider and withheld from driver pending review' (EV-TRIP-05069), and the payments ledger shows payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00 (EV-FARE-05069). The driver's filing asks the tribunal to move that 5.00 back to him. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative and never means 'restore a charge' - it means the filer's claim is not supported and the present state stands. The present state is a completed refund to the rider, and that is where the rider's case rests: the 5.00 refunded to her stays with her unless the driver positively makes out that the fee stands.

POL-NS-23 is the only limb of the driver's case that is not on the face of the platform record, and on that record it is thin. trip_record.in_app_calls is an empty array (EV-TRIP-05069), so no platform call record exists for this trip; the sole call evidence is one chat-log entry, MSG-05069-002 (EV-CHAT-05069), which records the call as 'Outgoing in-app call to rider - not answered (rang 24 s)'. The rider's statement on file - 'He never called me, he only sent messages' - is exactly what that entry says happened: a call was dialled and nothing was answered. The rider's account is therefore not a bare denial set against the record; it matches the record. On this evidence the driver has shown that he dialled, not that the rider was contacted, and the second limb of POL-NS-23 is not made out to the standard that would justify restoring a no-show fee against the rider.

If the tribunal reads POL-NS-23 as satisfied by a dialled-call line, the contact fact is still carried by no call record in the trip file at all: trip_record.in_app_calls is empty (EV-TRIP-05069) and the only support is a text entry in the chat log (EV-CHAT-05069). POL-GEN-26 sends a case to human review where a fact a rule needs cannot be established from the evidence that should carry it, and an escalated amount is held rather than collected - which leaves the rider's refunded 5.00 where it is and puts the driver's claim before a reviewer instead of restoring the charge on this record. I make that argument on completeness, not impairment: the chat log is graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and I do not suggest any issue code fired on it.

The driver was physically at the pickup when the arrival event fired. The platform trip record puts auto-arrival from driver GPS at 13:27:15 on 2026-09-17 at Block 216, Serangoon Avenue 4, and the GPS trace corroborates it: the nearest fix (index 12, 13:27:10) sits 0.497 m from the pickup point with a reported horizontal accuracy of 6 m, well inside the 50 m arrival radius that applies to a STANDARD pickup zone, and the trace reports accuracy on every fix so the 25 m accuracy filter is satisfied, not evaded. The arrival test under POL-NS-21 is therefore met on the platform's own evidence, at weight 1.0.

The free wait ran in full before the driver cancelled. Arrival at 13:27:15 starts the 300 s clock under POL-NS-21, so the free wait ended at 13:32:15; the platform logged 'free wait period expired; rider not on board' at 13:32:20 and the driver cancelled at 13:33:40, 385 s after arrival and 85 s after the wait expired. The trace shows the vehicle stationary at the pickup from 13:27:10 to 13:33:40 (speed 0 kph on every fix in that span), so the driver did not merely touch and go; he waited out the free period before cancelling. POL-NS-21 is satisfied and POL-NS-22's precondition - a driver cancellation after the free wait - is met.

The driver discharged the POL-NS-23 contact obligation in both limbs, before cancelling. He sent in-app chat messages at 13:27:40 (MSG-05069-001, 'Hi I'm at Blk 216 drop off') and 13:32:00 (MSG-05069-003, 'Hello?'), and he placed an in-app call at 13:30:15 (MSG-05069-002, channel VOICE_CALL_LOG, 'Outgoing in-app call to rider - not answered (rang 24 s)'). All three entries pre-date trip_record.cancelled_at of 13:33:40. POL-NS-23 expressly accepts 'a voice-call entry in the chat log' as the call limb, and the platform chat log is a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0 whose derived contact check records complete = true, call_count = 1 and obligation_met = true. The clause is satisfied and the fee is not voided.

The rider's counter-statement - 'He never called me, he only sent messages' - is contradicted by the platform's own voice-call record and does not defeat the contact obligation. POL-NS-23 requires that the driver place at least one in-app call, not that the rider answer it; the log records an outgoing call placed at 13:30:15 that rang for 24 s unanswered, which is precisely the situation the clause contemplates. The rider may not have registered the call, but the obligation is judged on the placed call, and the placed call is on the record at weight 1.0.

POL-NS-24 does not assist the rider here. That clause gives a rider a free cancellation only where the driver fails to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes and the rider then cancels; this trip was on-demand, it was cancelled by the driver and not by the rider, and the driver in fact arrived at 13:27:15. Nor can the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit under POL-NS-24 arise, because it is conditioned on a failure to attempt contact and the chat log records an attempted call as well as two messages. There is no driver no-show on this record.

The fee was correctly charged at the policy figure and belongs to the driver. The payments ledger records a 5.00 SGD cancellation fee, category NO_SHOW_CHARGE, with fee_matches_policy = true against the POL-NS-22 schedule of 5.00 SGD, and POL-NS-22 directs that a fee charged after a post-free-wait cancellation is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel. On the merits the driver is owed that 5.00 SGD, and under POL-GEN-03 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

NO_ACTION would be the wrong outcome and would simply entrench the error. The interim reversal at 13:25:40 (recorded as fee_reversed) refunded the 5.00 SGD to the rider and withheld it from the driver, pending this review. POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative: it means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands. Here the driver's claim IS supported - the free wait was served and the contact obligation was met - so leaving the present state standing would leave the driver 5.00 SGD out of pocket on a fee the policy awards him. The driver asks for DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, not for a further or separate payment.

Nothing in this record requires escalation. The two facts the no-show rules turn on - when the driver arrived, and whether he messaged and called before cancelling - are both established by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 (the platform trip record, the GPS trace and the chat log), so POL-GEN-26's condition, a fact the evidence cannot establish, is not met. The contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no 0.95 bar applies; and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling final on a 5.00 SGD no-show, subject only to POL-GEN-21, which is not engaged because no safety indicator appears anywhere on this record.
